subject.title: Add external event hooks for quota and provider state changes

question: Should CodexBar core adopt user-configured external command hooks as a supported long-term config, CLI, settings, event-payload, and local execution surface?
rationale: The patch is more than wiring: it establishes stable automation contracts and a persistent command-execution capability that cannot be approved from implementation quality alone.

options.title: Accept core hooks
options.body: Approve the surface after the argument round-trip defect is fixed and retain the documented shell-free, minimal-environment security boundary.

options.title: Narrow the first version
options.body: Accept only a smaller CLI/config-only event subset and defer the settings editor or less-established events until the contract is proven.

options.title: Decline core execution
options.body: Keep CodexBar observational and reject persistent external command execution from shared configuration.

recommendation.title: Accept core hooks
recommendation.body: Approve the surface after the argument round-trip defect is fixed and retain the documented shell-free, minimal-environment security boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository owner is the best available authority for a new durable product and security boundary spanning core config, app UI, and CLI.
